findings.text: The provenance line added at b6dd351a (lines 48-55) states that every number is 'rounded to five significant figures', but the table's cells are not: QAXIS +0.9989 is four significant figures (read 0.99886), Q95 +28.32 is four (read 28.3207), QSURF +97.62 is four (read 97.6188), while TTCU +353524 (read 353524) is six, unrounded. The cell values themselves now agree with the read; only the stated rounding rule is inaccurate. State the rounding actually applied, or round all cells uniformly to five significant figures.

The FAME table header still labels the two per-channel value columns 'first t' and 'last t', but the cells hold the first and last sample VALUES, not times (QAXIS +0.9989 / +0.9982, Q95 +28.32 / +7.287 are signed q). The read's own tool line labels the same two numbers simply 'first' and 'last'. Raised against b6a5eceb and unchanged at b6dd351a; relabel 'first'/'last' (values) or carry the sample times, so the header matches the cells.

The leads table states the Experiment Database Web API 'serves discharge and plant time series only ... not an equilibrium store', while the node's brief asked whether it serves EQDB or FAME records. The manual the node retrieved (pdftotext over /home/d240044/Code/jt60sa-agent/mindsdb/pdf/WEB API/WebAPI_UserGuide(rmssnd23)_EN_20240304.pdf, grepped for eqdb|fame|equilibrium) names the host rmssnd23.naka.qst.go.jp and port 50000 and describes the API as an interface 'for downloading data', but names neither EQDB nor FAME; 'not an equilibrium store' is the node's inference from the manual's download scope rather than the manual's statement, and should be qualified as such. Raised against b6a5eceb and unchanged at b6dd351a.

justifications.durability: The fragment is static HTML whose key result - the reached and unreached leads - is stated in its own text, and the run's negative_control.log is present and openable so the IRET 300 reproduction can be re-checked without the live host. The b6dd351a repair also adds a provenance line naming the read's own summary statistics, which helps a later reader re-derive the read. Deduction: the node keeps no named probe logs on disk for the FAME read, the per-shot EQDB index table, the LOCALDB listing or the Web API manual read - those live only inside the run's session transcript, so re-verifying the fragment's numbers means reading that transcript rather than a node-named log.
justifications.evidence: Every material claim traces to a call and its result in the run's on-disk session transcript: the FAME read returns 'SERVED 8 REFUSED 0' with each channel's first/last/min/max; the per-shot GetTimeList table matches the fragment row for row (E100999 63 / 1 1 1 1, E101029 94 / 2 2 2 2, E101162 126 / 9 9 9 9, E101163 48 / 4 4 4 4, E101154 105, eqdb=5 always 0); the Web API manual names host rmssnd23.naka.qst.go.jp;157.111.196.190 port 50000; the decommissioned FAME EQDB returns IRET 300 with the index resolving (105 slices), so the empty field return is shown to be an absence rather than a dead reader. The blocking finding of the b6a5eceb review - Q95 max asserted +32.65 against a read of 32.3899 - is corrected at b6dd351a, and the fix also caught TTCU first (353525 -> 353524); every cell now agrees with the read. Deductions: the provenance line's 'five significant figures' rule does not describe the cells; the FAME header still says 'first t'/'last t' over value cells; the Web API 'not an equilibrium store' conclusion is the node's inference.
justifications.fit: The deliverable is a data-reckon evidence fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-machine-map/, the form and location the machine-map plan uses for node evidence, and it opens with a scope statement naming the read-only host, the single home read (/home/d240034), and the negative control; nothing in it is out of place for the plan's evidence layer.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The brief's done-when is met item by item: each named lead carries what it holds (a grid, a q profile or signed q scalars), which OP1 shots it holds, and how intr26-2 reaches it, each with the exact call and result; the FAME q scalars are read through fetch_channels and their sign stated for E101154 beside the Ip and F.mB_T signs; the Web API's serving host is named from the manual on nakasvr26. Deduction: the FAME header mislabels the value columns and the Web API conclusion is an inference, so two of the stated facts are looser than the source supports.
justifications.reuse: No repository source is touched; the node reuses the existing ambix fetch_channels / RemoteEddbExtractor path and the prebuilt /analysis/lib/libFLEDDPIC.so reader rather than building a new one, and it names the existing jtmm-op1-shot-survey.json as a named evidence input, so the fragment layers onto the plan's evidence rather than duplicating it. Deduction: the same read is not captured to a durable named log a sibling node could reuse.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat of b6dd351a against b839dae7 lists exactly one changed file, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-machine-map/jtmm-equilibrium-source-leads.html, the manifest's declared changed_path and within the node's declared write scope; no source, test, plan or index is touched, the node is read-only on nakasvr26 with one ssh connection at a time, and the negative control is reproduced rather than assumed.
